key_insight: CARing improves next-visit diagnosis prediction by pairing compact semantic diagnosis tokens with training that rewards coverage of multiple correct diagnoses, not just repeated hits.
clinical_relevance: This could support more complete differential-style prediction from longitudinal EHRs, helping models cover co-occurring diagnoses more reliably in clinical NLP settings.
method: Represents diagnoses as compositional Semantic IDs (SIDs) learned from ontology-enriched disease semantics.
Aligns SID tokens with natural language and EHR context using multi-task and reasoning-enriched training.
Adds coverage-based reinforcement learning plus multi-positive supervision; supports constrained decoding and multi-chain rank fusion at inference.
evidence_signal: On MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, the method outperformed EHR-trained baselines in weighted F1 and achieved the best reported top-k recall, including R@30 of 46.04% and 46.52% in reasoning mode.
watch_item: The approach depends on ontology quality, token design, and careful inference constraints, so performance may vary when moving to different hospitals or coding systems.
paper_title: Coverage-Aware Reasoning with Medical Tokens for Diagnosis Prediction
